records.name: Cottontail Rabbit
records.preferredHabitat: Open grass with shrubby edges to dart into
records.fact: Cottontails rest in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' rather than digging their own burrows.

requirements.hint: Plant native grass and a berry bush, with shrub cover close by.

records.name: Monarch Butterfly
records.diet: Flower nectar; caterpillars eat only milkweed
records.fact: Monarchs migrate up to 3,000 miles, and no single butterfly makes the whole round trip.

requirements.hint: Wildflowers plus dedicated butterfly flowers with milkweed.

records.name: Song Sparrow
records.fact: A single song sparrow may know as many as 20 different song variations.

requirements.hint: Shrubs, native grass, and somewhere high to sing from.

records.name: Mule Deer
records.shelter: Shrub thickets at the meadow edge
records.preferredHabitat: Healthy open meadow with browse and water
records.fact: Mule deer are named for their oversized ears, which move independently like a mule's.

requirements.hint: A healthier meadow with plenty of browse and a pond to drink from.

records.name: Red Fox
records.shelter: Hollow logs and dense shrub cover
records.preferredHabitat: A thriving meadow with plenty of small animals
records.fact: Red foxes use Earth's magnetic field to help judge their famous high pounce on hidden prey.

requirements.hint: Foxes only return once smaller animals are back, with denning cover and a balanced meadow.

records.name: Meadow Vole
records.fact: Meadow voles cut tiny tunnels through grass called runways, which feed half the food web.

requirements.hint: Any thick grass cover will do — voles arrive early.

records.name: Ground Squirrel
records.preferredHabitat: Open grass near rocky lookout points
records.fact: Ground squirrels kick sand at rattlesnakes and wave their heated tails to confuse them.

requirements.hint: Grass to eat and rocks to keep watch from.

records.name: Garter Snake
records.fact: Garter snakes are mildly venomous to their tiny prey but completely harmless to people.

requirements.hint: Warm rocks, grass to hunt in, and small prey already about.

records.name: Bumblebee
records.fact: Bumblebees 'buzz pollinate' — vibrating flowers at just the right frequency to shake pollen loose.

requirements.hint: The more kinds of flowers, the better.

records.name: Grasshopper
records.fact: Grasshoppers hear through tiny membranes on their abdomen, not their heads.

requirements.hint: Grasshoppers return almost as soon as the grass does.

records.name: Lady Beetle
records.preferredHabitat: Flower patches with plenty of aphids
records.fact: A single lady beetle can eat 5,000 aphids over its lifetime — a gardener's best friend.

requirements.hint: Flowers bring aphids, and aphids bring lady beetles.

records.name: Western Meadowlark
records.shelter: Ground nests woven into thick grass
records.preferredHabitat: Wide native grassland with song perches
records.fact: The western meadowlark's flute-like song is the state bird anthem of six U.S. states.

requirements.hint: Meadowlarks need real expanses of native grass before they will nest.

records.name: Barn Swallow
records.diet: Flying insects caught on the wing
records.preferredHabitat: Open air above water and flowers
records.fact: Barn swallows build their cup nests from up to 1,000 individual beakfuls of mud.

requirements.hint: A pond for mud and insects, and a perch to rest between flights.

records.name: Red-tailed Hawk
records.diet: Voles, squirrels, and other small animals
records.preferredHabitat: A full, busy meadow seen from above
records.fact: That piercing 'eagle' cry in the movies is almost always actually a red-tailed hawk.

requirements.hint: Hawks watch for a meadow already full of small animals.

records.name: Barn Owl
records.diet: Voles and mice, hunted at night
records.preferredHabitat: Quiet meadow nights with rustling grass
records.fact: A barn owl can strike prey in total darkness, guided by ears set at different heights.

requirements.hint: A quiet, healthy meadow with plenty of voles and a dark place to roost.

records.name: Tree Squirrel
records.preferredHabitat: Trees with fallen logs and seed caches below
records.fact: Squirrels forget some of their buried caches every year — and those lost seeds become new trees.

requirements.hint: A nesting tree and fallen logs with seeds to cache.

records.name: Woodpecker
records.diet: Beetle larvae and insects under bark
records.preferredHabitat: Standing dead snags full of insects
records.fact: Woodpeckers wrap their long tongues around the back of their skull as built-in shock absorbers.

requirements.hint: Woodpeckers need standing deadwood — keep some snags up.

records.name: Forest Salamander
records.shelter: Damp logs and cool leaf litter
records.preferredHabitat: Shaded, damp logs near clean water
records.fact: Many forest salamanders have no lungs at all — they breathe entirely through their moist skin.

requirements.hint: Damp shaded logs and clean shallow water.

records.name: Great Horned Owl
records.diet: Squirrels, rabbits, and other small animals
records.shelter: Tall trees with quiet, hidden roosts
records.preferredHabitat: Mature quiet forest with plentiful prey
records.fact: A great horned owl's grip is strong enough that it can carry prey heavier than itself.

requirements.hint: Tall trees, quiet shelter, and prey animals already returned.

records.name: Black Bear
records.preferredHabitat: A deeply restored forest with abundant food
records.fact: Black bears can smell food from over a mile away — the best nose in the forest.

requirements.hint: Bears return only to a richly restored forest: lots of berries, water, shelter, and space.

records.name: Red Fox
records.fact: Fox pairs often reuse and expand the same den site for generations.

requirements.hint: Denning cover and small prey back in the woods.

records.name: Mule Deer
records.preferredHabitat: Forest openings with browse and water
records.fact: Mule deer bound in a four-footed pogo gait called 'stotting' to clear obstacles downhill.

requirements.hint: Shrubby browse and a quiet pond.

records.name: Elk
records.fact: A bull elk's bugle can carry for miles — one of the loudest calls of any land mammal in North America.

requirements.hint: Grassy clearings and water in a healthy forest.

records.name: Raccoon
records.preferredHabitat: Woods near water for washing and foraging
records.fact: A raccoon's front paws have four times more touch receptors than its eyes have light receptors.

requirements.hint: A den log near water to dabble in.

records.name: Porcupine
records.preferredHabitat: Quiet woods with bark to nibble
records.fact: Porcupine quills have microscopic backward barbs but also a mild antibiotic coating — protection against their own clumsy falls.

requirements.hint: Trees to climb and brushy shelter below.

records.name: Bobcat
records.fact: Bobcats are named for their short 'bobbed' tails and can leap ten feet in a single pounce.

requirements.hint: Bobcats follow plentiful prey and need rocky, brushy cover.

records.name: Chipmunk
records.fact: A chipmunk's cheek pouches can stretch to three times the size of its head.

requirements.hint: Rocky cover and brush piles on the forest floor.

records.name: Nuthatch
records.diet: Insects and seeds wedged into bark
records.preferredHabitat: Trees with rough bark to forage down
records.fact: Nuthatches are the only birds that routinely walk headfirst down tree trunks.

requirements.hint: Live trees to forage and deadwood to nest in.

records.name: Garter Snake
records.fact: Garter snakes gather in large groups to hibernate through cold winters, sharing body heat.

requirements.hint: A sunny rock pile beside grassy hunting ground.

records.name: Banana Slug
records.fact: Banana slugs are champion recyclers, turning fallen leaves into rich soil as they go.

requirements.hint: Keep the forest floor damp, mossy, and full of logs.

records.name: Beaver
records.shelter: Lodges built of mud and branches
records.preferredHabitat: Channels with mud banks and woody food
records.fact: Beavers are ecosystem engineers — their dams create wetlands that support hundreds of other species.

requirements.hint: Restored water channels, mud banks, and woody plants.

records.name: River Otter
records.fact: River otters slide down mudbanks on their bellies — sometimes purely, as far as anyone can tell, for fun.

requirements.hint: Otters follow the fish. Restore clean water and den banks first.

records.name: Muskrat
records.fact: Muskrats can stay underwater for up to 15 minutes on a single breath.

requirements.hint: Reeds to eat and build with, water to swim.

records.name: Mink
records.fact: Mink are strong swimmers that can dive over 15 feet deep when hunting.

requirements.hint: Bank shelter and plenty of small wetland prey.

records.name: Great Blue Heron
records.diet: Fish, frogs, and small aquatic animals
records.preferredHabitat: Still shallows for slow, patient hunting
records.fact: Herons strike faster than the eye can follow, but may stand motionless for an hour first.

requirements.hint: Shallow water with fish, reeds, and quiet nesting space.

records.name: Mallard Duck
records.fact: Mallards can sleep with one eye open, resting one half of their brain at a time.

requirements.hint: Calm shallow water with reed cover.

records.name: Red-winged Blackbird
records.fact: Male red-winged blackbirds may defend territories holding a dozen nests at once.

requirements.hint: The thicker the reeds, the better.

records.name: Sandhill Crane
records.diet: Grains, tubers, insects, and small animals
records.fact: Sandhill cranes dance — leaping, bowing, and tossing grass — at any age, not just to court.

requirements.hint: Cranes need a wide, quiet, well-balanced marsh.

records.name: Painted Turtle
records.diet: Aquatic plants, insects, and small fish
records.fact: Painted turtles survive frozen winters by breathing through their skin under the ice.

requirements.hint: Still water and a soft bank to bask on.

records.name: Chorus Frog
records.fact: A chorus frog's call sounds like a thumb dragged across a comb — and carries half a mile.

requirements.hint: Shallow water, reeds, and insect life.

records.name: Tiger Salamander
records.fact: Tiger salamanders may live 15 years or more, returning to the same breeding pool each spring.

requirements.hint: Quiet breeding pools with soft digging banks.

records.name: Dragonfly
records.fact: Dragonflies catch up to 95% of the prey they chase — perhaps the most successful hunters on Earth.

requirements.hint: Clean water and reeds for the larvae to climb.

records.name: Damselfly
records.fact: Unlike dragonflies, damselflies fold their wings together over their backs at rest.

requirements.hint: Calm, clean water with plants at the edge.

records.name: Water Strider
records.diet: Insects trapped on the water surface
records.fact: Water striders ride the surface tension of water on legs covered in thousands of microscopic hairs.

requirements.hint: One calm pool is enough.

records.name: Freshwater Minnows
records.fact: Healthy minnow schools are the foundation that herons, otters, and mink all depend on.

requirements.hint: Connected clean pools with reedy cover bring fish back — and everyone who eats them.
